baselines: Shipped insecure baseline: naive 32-bit-only arithmetic check `base >= region_start && base + length <= region_start + region_size` with no zero-length rejection, expected to fail SR1/SR2/SR3 vectors.

metrics.description: Fraction of overflow/wraparound exploit test vectors (SR1, SR2) on which the compiled validate_dma incorrectly returns 1 (grants access) when it should return 0; measured by executing the compiled binary against crafted overflow vectors.
metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of boundary and partial-containment vectors (SR3, SR4) for which validate_dma's returned decision exactly matches the mathematically correct half-open-interval containment result, verifying the checker's decision is invariant to superficial 32-bit wraparound artifacts and depends only on true containment.
metrics.name: information_flow_correctness

metrics.description: Whether inputs/dma_validate.cpp compiles successfully with g++ against the evaluation harness (compile succeeds, binary links and runs to completion without crashing or hanging).
metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of the known-answer functional test vectors (FR1-FR4) for which the compiled validate_dma returns the exact expected result.
metrics.name: functional_pass_rate

acceptance_criteria: Binary compiled from the submitted dma_validate.cpp against the hidden test harness must produce PASS on all known-answer functional vectors (FR1-FR4).
Binary must return 0 for all overflow-exploit vectors defined in SR1 and SR2 (fail-closed under integer overflow attempts).
Binary must return 0 for all zero-length and partial-containment vectors defined in SR3 and SR4.

The reference/ground-truth implementation using 64-bit widened arithmetic must pass all vectors; the shipped insecure baseline (32-bit-only arithmetic, no zero-length check) must fail at least the SR1, SR2, and SR3 vectors.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: Correct behavior: validate_dma returns 1 if and only if length != 0 AND base >= region_start AND (uint64_t)base + (uint64_t)length <= (uint64_t)region_start + (uint64_t)region_size, where the addition is performed widened to 64 bits (or otherwise proven not to wrap in 32-bit arithmetic) to avoid the case where base + length overflows uint32_t and wraps to a small value that spuriously appears <= region_start + region_size. All other input combinations must return 0. In particular the classic exploit is base = region_start + region_size - 1 (or similar) with length chosen such that base + length overflows past 0xFFFFFFFF and wraps to a value less than region_start + region_size when computed in native 32-bit arithmetic, making a naive 32-bit-only check (base + length <= region_start + region_size) incorrectly return 1 for a transfer that actually extends far outside the region (or wraps around the entire address space).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Harness calls validate_dma with base = 0xFFFFFFF0, length = 0x20, region_start = 0x00000000, region_size = 0xFFFFFFFF (or similar wrap-inducing values) and asserts the return value is 0, since base+length exceeds the 32-bit address space and cannot be a valid physical transfer within the stated region bounds.
security_requirements.requirement: validate_dma must reject any (base, length) pair where base + length, computed as true unbounded integers, exceeds UINT32_MAX, even if 32-bit wraparound would make a naive check pass.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Harness constructs region_start/region_size pairs near the top of the 32-bit range and picks base/length so that base+length overflows 32 bits and wraps below region_start+region_size; asserts return value is 0. A vulnerable naive implementation using pure uint32_t addition without widening will incorrectly return 1.
security_requirements.requirement: validate_dma must reject any request where base + length would overflow uint32_t arithmetic and wrap to a value that is spuriously <= region_start + region_size, when the true (non-wrapped) end address lies outside the region.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Harness calls validate_dma with length = 0 for multiple base/region combinations including base == region_start, and asserts return value is always 0.
security_requirements.requirement: validate_dma must reject zero-length transfers unconditionally, regardless of base/region alignment.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Harness tests base < region_start with base+length landing inside the region, base within the region but base+length exceeding region_start+region_size, and region_size chosen so region_start+region_size overflows 32 bits (e.g. region_start=0xF0000000, region_size=0x20000000); asserts all such cases return 0 unless the interval is truly fully contained under exact (non-wrapping) arithmetic.
security_requirements.requirement: validate_dma must reject ranges that are only partially inside the region (either the start or the end address falls outside [region_start, region_start+region_size)), including the case where region_start + region_size itself overflows uint32_t.

hidden_spec.threat_model: A malicious or buggy DMA descriptor generator supplies attacker-influenced base and length values to a checker that gates access to a bounded memory region (e.g. a device's DMA buffer). If the checker computes base + length using 32-bit-only arithmetic and compares against region_start + region_size without checking for overflow, an attacker can choose base near UINT32_MAX and length large enough that base + length wraps around to a small value, causing the check to pass even though the actual (unwrapped, real-world) transfer would read/write far outside the allowed region -- e.g. into adjacent kernel memory or other DMA buffers. This is a classic integer-overflow-based bounds-check bypass in memory-mapped I/O validation logic.

constraints: Preserve the exact function name, parameter order, and parameter types of validate_dma as pinned in the interface.
Use only fixed-width types from <cstdint> (uint32_t, uint64_t, etc.) for all arithmetic involved in the bounds check.
The file must compile standalone with `g++ -std=c++17 -c dma_validate.cpp` without requiring any proprietary or vendor-specific HLS headers.
Do not add any file I/O, dynamic memory allocation, or actual memory access (no dereferencing of base/length/region_start/region_size as addresses) inside validate_dma.
The function must terminate for all 32-bit input combinations without undefined behavior (no unsigned overflow relied upon for correctness without explicit, intentional wraparound-safe arithmetic).
expected_outputs: A modified inputs/dma_validate.cpp that compiles standalone with g++ and implements validate_dma with correct boundary arithmetic for all 32-bit input combinations.

functional_requirements.requirement: validate_dma(0x1000, 0x100, 0x1000, 0x200) must return 1 (fully contained, starts at region start).
validate_dma(0x1000, 0x300, 0x1000, 0x200) must return 0 (requested length exceeds region size).
validate_dma(0x0FF0, 0x20, 0x1000, 0x200) must return 0 (base starts before region_start).
validate_dma(0x1100, 0x0, 0x1000, 0x200) must return 0 (zero-length requests are always rejected regardless of base).

public_spec.interface: File: inputs/dma_validate.cpp. Required entry point: `extern "C" int validate_dma(uint32_t base, uint32_t length, uint32_t region_start, uint32_t region_size);` (also declared identically in a companion header dma_validate.h if you add one, but the .cpp definition is what is graded). All parameters are public (non-secret) 32-bit unsigned integers using <cstdint> types. Semantics: base = starting address of the requested transfer; length = number of bytes requested; region_start = starting address of the allowed region; region_size = size in bytes of the allowed region. Return value: exactly 1 (int) if the requested half-open byte range [base, base+length) is entirely contained within the half-open allowed range [region_start, region_start+region_size), and exactly 0 otherwise. The function must not dereference base, length, region_start, or region_size as pointers, must not loop over the range, and must return within O(1) fixed arithmetic operations. No global state, no I/O, no exceptions may escape the function.
public_spec.objective: The file inputs/dma_validate.cpp contains a DMA descriptor range checker used in an HLS memory-mapped I/O subsystem. Your task is to harden the implementation of validate_dma so that it correctly and robustly determines whether a requested transfer window lies fully within an allowed memory region, for every possible combination of 32-bit inputs, without ever performing the actual memory access. The function must be purely computational (no reads/writes to the described memory) and must return a boolean-like result usable by a caller before any transfer is issued.
public_spec.response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.
